gen-dafont-oldtimer-nunito-sans: Round, stately, and unshaded: Oldtimer. Nunito Sans follows in a sans with soft, open-mouthed curves, so a long page of text feels gentle after that commanding heading.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-amulya: Origami looks brushed on by a sign painter, one constant width throughout. Amulya, a plain sans, sits lower and more modest in its lowercase, with generous gaps in its curves, so the heavy heading towers over a lighter, more spacious text.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-chillax: Chillax reads loose and relaxed, its lines like spaghetti with loops left unfinished. Against Origami's dense, high lowercase, the pair's strongest quality is that tension between a heavy brushed heading and a wandering, easygoing body.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-plein: Contemporary and a bit unusual, Origami brings a single-stroke brush look and a dense lowercase to the top. And Plein, a plain sans with a clear channel leading into each round letter, stays lower and tidier, so the heading can be sized well above it.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-spline-sans: A sign-painter's brush stroke at constant width, with lowercase as dense as poured lead, defines Origami. Spline Sans answers with wide-open curves and a friendlier, lower build.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-synonym: Synonym reads as a plain stripe of ink with generous openings in every curve, lower and quieter than its heading. Origami's dense, high lowercase gives a long page a strong top note.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-almendra: Brushed and dense, like poured lead. Origami handles the loud, constant-width display work, while Almendra, a text serif with a deep midsection in its lowercase, does the dignified, bookish reading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-bree-serif: Origami keeps one constant stroke from top to baseline, brush-like and tall. Its strongest quality against Bree Serif is the clash with that text serif's outsized, literary lowercase.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-port-lligat-slab: Port Lligat Slab reads traditional and literary, its lowercase counters like wide glass portholes with open-ended curves. And Origami, a constant-width trace like a laser-etched line, gives it a sharp, modern heading above.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-quando: Bookish and traditional, Quando spaces its letters sparsely and lifts a big, tall middle zone into every word. Origami is the louder one, its rod-stock strokes best at display, while the serif does the reading.
